people.name: Gustav Kirchhoff
people.bio: German physicist who formulated the circuit laws and, with Bunsen, founded spectrum analysis.

stops.note: Attended the Neumann–Jacobi mathematics-physics seminar; graduated 1847.

people.name: Alexander Borodin
people.bio: Russian chemist and composer, professor at the St Petersburg Medico-Surgical Academy and member of 'The Five'.

stops.note: Studied at the Medico-Surgical Academy, specialising in chemistry; doctorate 1858.
Adjunct professor of chemistry from 1862, full professor 1864. The roster's 1850 start includes his student years.

people.name: William Stanley Jevons
people.bio: English economist and logician, a founder of marginal utility theory.

stops.note: Studied natural sciences at University College; broke off in 1854.
Resumed studies at University College after returning to England.
Tutor, then from 1866 professor of political economy at Owens College.
Professor of political economy at University College.

people.name: Giosuè Carducci
people.bio: Italian poet and literary scholar, Nobel laureate in literature (1906).

stops.note: Professor of Italian literature for more than 40 years.

people.name: William Henry Perkin
people.bio: English chemist who discovered mauve, the first synthetic aniline dye.

stops.note: Studied under A. W. von Hofmann, then his laboratory assistant.
Ran an aniline dye works near Harrow.

people.name: Josif Pančić
people.bio: Croatian-born Serbian botanist and physician, first president of the Serbian Royal Academy.

stops.note: Studied medicine and natural science at Pest; MD 1843.
A year at the Natural History Museum.
Professor of natural sciences at the Lyceum (later the Great School). Source dates appointment to about 1851.

people.name: Joseph Sadler
people.bio: Hungarian botanist and physician who taught botany at the University of Pest.

people.name: Camillo Golgi
people.bio: Italian histologist who devised the silver-staining 'black reaction'; Nobel laureate in medicine (1906).

stops.note: Worked at the Hospital of St Matteo.
Chief medical officer of the hospital for the chronically sick.
Professor of histology, then from 1881 general pathology; also rector. A brief spell at Siena is not dated by the source.

people.name: Giulio Bizzozero
people.bio: Italian pathologist and histologist at Pavia and Turin, who discovered blood platelets.

people.name: Paolo Mantegazza
people.bio: Italian physician and anthropologist who taught pathology at Pavia.

people.name: Ivan Pavlov
people.bio: Russian physiologist known for conditioned reflexes; Nobel laureate in medicine (1904).

stops.note: Faculty of physics and mathematics; candidate of natural sciences 1875.
Studied at the Medico-Surgical (later Military Medical) Academy, completing 1879.
Fellow of the Academy; ran the physiological laboratory at S. P. Botkin's clinic.
Professor of pharmacology, then of physiology (to 1925); from 1890 also directed physiology at the Institute of Experimental Medicine.

people.name: Ilya Mechnikov
people.bio: Russian zoologist and immunologist who discovered phagocytosis; Nobel laureate in medicine (1908).

stops.note: Born in a village near Kharkiv.
Studied natural sciences, finishing the four-year course in two.
Doctoral research on embryology; also worked in Göttingen and Munich.
Docent at the new university, then briefly at St Petersburg.
Professor of zoology and comparative anatomy.
Private laboratory where he observed phagocytosis.
Directed the Odessa bacteriological institute for Pasteur's rabies treatment.

people.name: Rudolf Leuckart
people.bio: German zoologist and parasitologist, professor at Giessen and Leipzig.

people.name: Svante Arrhenius
people.bio: Swedish physical chemist who developed the theory of electrolytic dissociation; Nobel laureate in chemistry (1903).

stops.note: Worked under E. Edlund at the Academy of Sciences; doctorate at Uppsala 1884.
Lecturer, from 1895 professor of physics, rector 1897–1905.
Head of the Nobel Institute for Physical Chemistry.

people.name: Jacobus van 't Hoff
people.bio: Dutch chemist, founder of stereochemistry and chemical thermodynamics; first Nobel laureate in chemistry (1901).

stops.note: Lecturer, then from 1878 professor of chemistry, mineralogy and geology.
Honorary professor attached to the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

people.name: Adolphe Wurtz
people.bio: French chemist at the Paris Faculty of Medicine and Sorbonne, leading advocate of atomic theory.

people.name: Eduard Mulder
people.bio: Dutch chemist, professor at Utrecht.

people.name: Wilhelm Ostwald
people.bio: Baltic German chemist, a founder of physical chemistry; Nobel laureate in chemistry (1909).

stops.note: Studied chemistry (exams 1875), then assistant and from 1877 Privatdozent at Dorpat.
Professor of chemistry at the Polytechnicum.
Died at his country house near Leipzig.

people.name: Carl Schmidt
people.bio: Baltic German chemist, professor at Dorpat.

people.name: Arthur von Oettingen
people.bio: Baltic German physicist and music theorist, professor at Dorpat.

people.name: Johannes van der Waals
people.bio: Dutch physicist known for the equation of state of real gases; Nobel laureate in physics (1910).

stops.note: Studied in his spare time; teaching certificates in mathematics and physics.
Teacher, later director of a secondary school; doctorate 1873.
First professor of physics. Source gives 1876 for the start.

people.name: Hendrik Lorentz
people.bio: Dutch theoretical physicist of electron theory; Nobel laureate in physics (1902).

stops.note: Curator of Teyler's physical cabinet; extraordinary professor at Leiden.

people.name: J. J. Thomson
people.bio: English physicist who discovered the electron; Nobel laureate in physics (1906).

people.name: Pierre Curie
people.bio: French physicist of piezoelectricity, magnetism and radioactivity; Nobel laureate in physics (1903).

stops.note: Licence in physics at the Faculty of Sciences, 1878.
Head of practical work, from 1895 professor of physics at the School of Physics and Industrial Chemistry.
Professor at the Faculty of Sciences; titular chair 1904.

people.name: Karl Weierstrass
people.bio: German mathematician who put analysis on rigorous foundations and taught a generation of mathematicians in Berlin.

stops.note: Studied finance and law; left without examinations.
Theological and Philosophical Academy; studied under Christoph Gudermann; teacher's examination 1840.
Professor of mathematics at the university.

people.name: Christoph Gudermann
people.bio: German mathematician at the Münster Academy, known for work on elliptic functions and as Weierstrass's teacher.

people.name: Georg Cantor
people.bio: German mathematician who created set theory and the theory of transfinite numbers.

stops.note: Polytechnic; cut short by his father's death.
Attended lectures by Weierstrass, Kummer and Kronecker; doctorate 1867 (summer 1866 at Göttingen).
Habilitation 1869, extraordinary professor 1872, full professor 1879; retired 1913.

people.name: Ernst Kummer
people.bio: German mathematician of number theory (ideal numbers), professor at Breslau and Berlin.

people.name: Leopold Kronecker
people.bio: German mathematician of number theory and algebra who lectured at the University of Berlin.

people.name: Felix Klein
people.bio: German mathematician of the Erlangen Program, who made Göttingen a world centre of mathematics.

stops.note: Studied mathematics and physics; assistant to Plücker; doctorate 1868.
Study visits to Berlin, Paris and Göttingen; met Sophus Lie.

people.name: Julius Plücker
people.bio: German mathematician and physicist at Bonn, pioneer of line geometry and cathode-ray studies.

people.name: David Hilbert
people.bio: German mathematician of invariant theory, foundations of geometry and the famous 1900 problem list.

stops.note: Doctorate under Ferdinand von Lindemann (1885); one semester at Heidelberg.
Second semester; attended lectures by Lazarus Fuchs.
Visits to Klein in Leipzig and to Poincaré and Hermite in Paris.

people.name: Ferdinand von Lindemann
people.bio: German mathematician who proved π transcendental; professor at Freiburg, Königsberg and Munich.

people.name: Hermann Minkowski
people.bio: German mathematician of the geometry of numbers and of four-dimensional spacetime.

stops.note: Taught about two years. The roster's 1880–85 stint is his student period.

people.name: Sofia Kovalevskaya
people.bio: Russian mathematician, the first woman to hold a full professorship in mathematics in modern Europe.

stops.note: Private lessons; attended Sechenov's physiology lectures.
Unofficially attended lectures by Kirchhoff, Helmholtz and Königsberger.
Private tuition by Weierstrass; doctorate from Göttingen in absentia 1874.

people.name: Gösta Mittag-Leffler
people.bio: Swedish mathematician, founder of Acta Mathematica and first mathematics professor at Stockholm University College.

stops.note: First professor of mathematics at Stockholms Högskola.

people.name: Charles Hermite
people.bio: French mathematician of number theory and elliptic functions, professor at the Sorbonne and École Polytechnique.

people.name: Henri Poincaré
people.bio: French mathematician and physicist, founder of topology and the qualitative theory of dynamical systems.

stops.note: École des Mines; doctorate at the University of Paris 1879 under Hermite.
Faculty of Sciences; chair of mathematical physics 1886.

people.name: Giuseppe Peano
people.bio: Italian mathematician and logician known for the axioms of arithmetic.

stops.note: Assistant to D'Ovidio and Genocchi, then professor (1890).

people.name: Angelo Genocchi
people.bio: Italian mathematician of number theory, professor at Turin.

people.name: Enrico D'Ovidio
people.bio: Italian geometer, professor at Turin.

people.name: Vito Volterra
people.bio: Italian mathematician of functional analysis and integral equations.

stops.note: Physics teacher (assistant) at the Istituto di Studi Superiori.
Laurea 1882 under Enrico Betti; Scuola Normale from 1879.
Assistant, professor of rational mechanics 1883, chair of mathematical physics 1892.
Chair of mathematical physics; dismissed after refusing the Fascist oath.

people.name: Enrico Betti
people.bio: Italian mathematician, professor at Pisa and director of the Scuola Normale.

people.name: Ulisse Dini
people.bio: Italian mathematician of real analysis, professor at Pisa.

people.name: Aleksandr Lyapunov
people.bio: Russian mathematician who founded the theory of stability of motion.

stops.note: Faculty of physics and mathematics, taught by Chebyshev; master's thesis 1884–85.

people.name: Gottlob Frege
people.bio: German logician and philosopher, founder of modern mathematical logic.

stops.note: Taught by Ernst Abbe and Kuno Fischer.
Privatdozent 1874, extraordinary professor 1879, honorary ordinary professor after 1893.

people.name: Elwin Christoffel
people.bio: German mathematician and physicist known for the Christoffel symbols in differential geometry.

stops.note: Taught by Dirichlet, Steiner, Eisenstein and others; doctorate 1856.

people.name: Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet
people.bio: German mathematician of analytic number theory and Fourier series, professor at Berlin and Göttingen.

people.name: Francesco Brioschi
people.bio: Italian mathematician and engineer, founder of the Politecnico di Milano.

stops.note: Doctorate 1845, thesis directed by Antonio Bordoni.
Secretary of the Ministry of Education.

people.name: Antonio Bordoni
people.bio: Italian mathematician and engineer, professor at Pavia.

people.name: Rudolf Clausius
people.bio: German physicist who formulated the second law of thermodynamics and introduced entropy.

stops.note: Docent; also professor at the Royal Artillery and Engineering School.
Professor of mathematical physics at the Polytechnikum and the University.

people.name: William John Macquorn Rankine
people.bio: Scottish engineer and physicist, a founder of thermodynamics and engineering science.

stops.note: Apprentice engineer to J. B. MacNeill in Scotland and Ireland.
Regius Professor of Civil Engineering and Mechanics.

people.name: Richard Dedekind
people.bio: German mathematician of algebraic number theory and the construction of the real numbers.

stops.note: Doctorate 1852 under Gauss; habilitation 1854, then taught.

people.name: Sophus Lie
people.bio: Norwegian mathematician who created the theory of continuous transformation groups (Lie groups).

stops.note: Science course; attended Sylow's lectures; graduated 1865.
Met Kummer, Kronecker, Weierstrass and Felix Klein.
With Klein; arrested at Fontainebleau as a suspected spy.

people.name: Ludwig Sylow
people.bio: Norwegian mathematician of group theory (Sylow theorems).

people.name: Ludwig Boltzmann
people.bio: Austrian physicist who founded statistical mechanics.

stops.note: Chair of theoretical physics, succeeding Stefan. MacTutor does not detail 1890–94 (Munich).
Theoretical physics; also took over Mach's philosophy course.

people.name: Josef Stefan
people.bio: Slovene-Austrian physicist of the Stefan–Boltzmann radiation law, professor at Vienna.

people.name: Heinrich Hertz
people.bio: German physicist who proved the existence of electromagnetic waves.

stops.note: University of Munich, with courses at the Technische Hochschule.
Studied under Helmholtz and Kirchhoff; doctorate 1880.
Assistant to Helmholtz at the Physical Institute.
Extraordinary professor at the Technische Hochschule.

people.name: Albert Einstein
people.bio: German-born physicist who developed the theories of relativity; Nobel laureate in physics (1921).

stops.note: Graduated as teacher of mathematics and physics.
Teacher at Winterthur and a private school in Schaffhausen.
Technical expert at the Patent Office; doctorate from Zurich 1905; lecturer at Bern 1908.
Full professor at the (German) Karl-Ferdinand University.
Berlin Academy research post with a university chair.

people.name: Max Planck
people.bio: German theoretical physicist who originated quantum theory; Nobel laureate in physics (1918).

stops.note: Universities of Munich and Berlin; doctorate at Munich 1879.
President of the Kaiser Wilhelm Society.

people.name: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen
people.bio: German physicist who discovered X-rays; first Nobel laureate in physics (1901).

stops.note: Technical school (expelled); briefly at Utrecht University 1865.
Mechanical engineering at the Polytechnic; attended Clausius's lectures and worked in Kundt's laboratory; PhD University of Zurich 1869.
Professor at the Academy of Agriculture.

people.name: Wilhelm Röntgen
people.bio: German physicist who discovered X-rays; first Nobel laureate in physics (1901). (Duplicate roster entry of Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen.)

stops.note: Technical school (expelled); briefly at Utrecht University 1865.
Mechanical engineering at the Polytechnic; attended Clausius's lectures and worked in Kundt's laboratory; PhD University of Zurich 1869.
Professor at the Academy of Agriculture.

people.name: August Kundt
people.bio: German experimental physicist at Zurich, Würzburg, Strasbourg and Berlin.

people.name: Jacob Burckhardt
people.bio: Swiss historian of art and culture, author of The Civilization of the Renaissance in Italy.

stops.note: Learned French with the Godet family.
Theology under Hagenbach and De Wette.
Lectures of Droysen, Ranke, Boeckh, Kugler and Grimm; Ranke's seminar; doctorate (Basel) 1843.
Summer term; heard F. G. Welcker.
Habilitation 1844, extraordinary professor 1845; with periods in Berlin (1846–47) and Italy.
Professor of art history at the new Polytechnikum.
Professor of history (to 1886) and art history (to 1893).

people.name: Franz Kugler
people.bio: German art historian at Berlin, author of handbooks of art history.

people.name: Gottfried Semper
people.bio: German architect and theorist (Dresden Opera, Vienna museums), professor at the Zurich Polytechnikum.

stops.note: Studied classical architecture in Italy and Greece.
Exile in Paris and London after the 1849 uprising.
Head of the architecture department of the Polytechnikum.
Rebuilding of Vienna; museums and Burgtheater.

people.name: Francesco De Sanctis
people.bio: Italian literary critic and historian of Italian literature, minister of education.

stops.note: After the 1848 revolution, imprisoned by the Bourbons for some years.
Lecturer at the Polytechnikum during exile.

people.name: José Echegaray
people.bio: Spanish engineer, mathematician, statesman and dramatist; Nobel laureate in literature (1904).

stops.note: Professor of mathematics in early life (roster dates).

people.name: Dmitri Mendeleev
people.bio: Russian chemist who formulated the periodic law and table of the elements.

stops.note: Professor at the Technological Institute 1864 and the university from 1865 (tenured 1867); resigned 1890.
Director of the Bureau of Weights and Measures.

people.name: Claude Bernard
people.bio: French physiologist, founder of experimental medicine and of the concept of the internal environment.

stops.note: Jesuit school, then college in Lyon.
Medicine; interne at the Hôtel-Dieu, where he met Magendie.
Préparateur to Magendie from 1841, deputy professor from 1847.
First chair of physiology at the Sorbonne.
Professor at the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle.

people.name: François Magendie
people.bio: French physiologist, pioneer of experimental physiology at the Collège de France.

people.name: Thomas Henry Huxley
people.bio: English biologist and educator, known as 'Darwin's bulldog' for his defence of evolution.

stops.note: Sydenham College, then Charing Cross Hospital; First MB, University of London.
Assistant surgeon on HMS Rattlesnake in Australian waters.
Professor of natural history at the Royal School of Mines (to 1885); naturalist to the Geological Survey from 1855.
Dean and professor of biology at the Normal School of Science (roster dates).

people.name: Ignaz Semmelweis
people.bio: Hungarian physician who showed that hand disinfection prevents puerperal fever.

stops.note: First Obstetrical Clinic of the Vienna General Hospital, assistant to Johann Klein; docent 1850.
Honorary head physician of the obstetric ward at St Rochus Hospital.
Died in the asylum at Döbling.

people.name: August Kekulé
people.bio: German chemist who founded structural theory and proposed the ring structure of benzene.

stops.note: Turned from architecture to chemistry under Justus von Liebig; doctorate 1852.

people.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
people.bio: German philosopher and classical philologist, critic of morality and religion.

stops.note: Grew up in Naumburg after his father's death.
Itinerant years in Switzerland, Italy and southern France.
Collapsed in Turin in January 1889; then cared for by his mother and sister.

people.name: Friedrich Ritschl
people.bio: German classical philologist at Bonn and Leipzig.

people.name: Ernst Haeckel
people.bio: German zoologist and popularizer of Darwinism who coined 'ecology' and 'phylum'.

stops.note: Medicine at Berlin and Würzburg (Kölliker, Leydig, Virchow, Müller); MD 1857.
Habilitation 1861; professor of zoology 1862–1909; studied under Carl Gegenbaur there.

people.name: Carl Gegenbaur
people.bio: German comparative anatomist at Jena and Heidelberg.

people.name: Johannes Müller
people.bio: German physiologist and comparative anatomist at Bonn and Berlin.

people.name: Ernest Renan
people.bio: French philologist, historian of religion and author of the Life of Jesus.

stops.note: Saint-Nicolas-du-Chardonnet, then Saint-Sulpice seminary (Hebrew and philology); left 1845; agrégé 1847.
Professor of Hebrew; administrator in his last years.

people.name: Henry Roscoe
people.bio: English chemist who isolated vanadium and built up the chemistry school at Owens College, Manchester.

stops.note: Chair of chemistry at Owens College (roster: to 1885).
Member of Parliament for Manchester South; vice-chancellor of the University of London 1896–1902.

people.name: Ivan Sechenov
people.bio: Russian physiologist, founder of Russian physiology and of the reflex theory of mind.

stops.note: Studied abroad with Müller, du Bois-Reymond and Helmholtz (Berlin), Hoppe-Seyler (Leipzig), Carl Ludwig (Vienna) and Claude Bernard (Paris).
Professor of physiology at the Medico-Surgical Academy; resigned 1870 over the rejection of Mechnikov.

people.name: Carl Ludwig
people.bio: German physiologist at Marburg, Zurich, Vienna and Leipzig, teacher of many foreign physiologists.

people.name: Sergey Botkin
people.bio: Russian clinician who founded scientific internal medicine in Russia.

stops.note: Military surgeon in the Crimean War under Pirogov.
Professor of clinical medicine at the Medico-Surgical Academy.

people.name: Stanislao Cannizzaro
people.bio: Italian chemist who revived Avogadro's hypothesis to fix atomic weights.

stops.note: Studied medicine at Palermo and Naples.
Artillery officer and deputy in the Sicilian revolution.
Professor of physical chemistry at the National College.

people.name: Raffaele Piria
people.bio: Italian chemist at Pisa and Turin who first prepared salicylic acid.

people.name: August Weismann
people.bio: German biologist who formulated the germ-plasm theory of heredity.

stops.note: Personal physician to Archduke Stephen of Austria; also worked with Leuckart at Giessen.
Privatdozent 1863, extraordinary professor 1866, first chair of zoology 1873–1912.

people.name: Ernst Abbe
people.bio: German physicist whose optical theory underpinned the Carl Zeiss works at Jena.

stops.note: PhD 1861 under Wilhelm Weber and Karl Snell's supervision; influenced by Riemann.
Lecturer 1863, professor 1870, observatory director 1878; relieved of teaching 1891 (roster: to 1896).
Research director at Zeiss; partner 1876; head of the firm from 1888.

people.name: Franz Reuleaux
people.bio: German mechanical engineer, founder of the kinematics of machines.

stops.note: Polytechnic school under Ferdinand Redtenbacher; then Berlin and Bonn universities.
Professor at the Swiss Federal Polytechnic.
Professor of kinematics at the Gewerbeakademie; director from 1868.
Professor and rector of the Technische Hochschule Charlottenburg.

people.name: Carl von Linde
people.bio: German engineer who developed refrigeration and the liquefaction of air.

stops.note: Studied under Clausius, Zeuner and Reuleaux; expelled 1864 after a student protest.
Worked at Kempten, Borsig in Berlin and the Krauss locomotive works in Munich.
Lecturer, full professor of mechanical engineering 1872.

people.name: Rudolf Diesel
people.bio: German engineer who invented the compression-ignition (diesel) engine.

stops.note: Vocational and industrial schools in Augsburg.
Royal Bavarian Polytechnic; graduated January 1880; student of Carl von Linde.
Linde's refrigeration plant; director about a year later.
Developed his engine at Maschinenfabrik Augsburg.
Vanished from the SS Dresden between Antwerp and London.

people.name: Carl Benz
people.bio: German engineer who built the first practical petrol-engined automobile (1885–86).

stops.note: Draftsman and designer at a scales factory.
Engineer at Gebrüder Benckiser; also briefly in Vienna.
Co-founded an iron foundry and mechanical workshop.

people.name: Gustav Zeuner
people.bio: German engineer and thermodynamicist at the Zurich Polytechnikum and Dresden.

people.name: Osborne Reynolds
people.bio: British engineer and physicist of fluid dynamics (Reynolds number).

stops.note: Civil engineer with Lawson and Mansergh.
Professor of civil and mechanical engineering at Owens College.

people.name: Oliver Lodge
people.bio: British physicist, pioneer of radio and first principal of the University of Birmingham.

stops.note: BSc 1875, DSc 1877, University of London; physics lectures in London.
Assistant professor of applied mathematics at Bedford College.
Professor of physics and mathematics at University College Liverpool.
Principal of the University of Birmingham.

people.name: Galileo Ferraris
people.bio: Italian physicist and electrical engineer who discovered the rotating magnetic field.

stops.note: Assistant, then professor of technical physics at the Industrial Museum; electrotechnical school 1889.

people.name: Alexander Popov
people.bio: Russian physicist, a pioneer of radio reception (1895).

stops.note: Physics; graduated with honours 1882, then laboratory assistant.
Teacher and laboratory head at the navy's Torpedo School.
Professor at the Electrotechnical Institute; director 1905.

people.name: Loránd Eötvös
people.bio: Hungarian physicist known for the torsion balance and tests of the equivalence of inertial and gravitational mass.

stops.note: Switched from law to physics; PhD at Heidelberg.
Professor of physics; president of the Academy 1889–1905; minister of education 1894–95.

people.name: Clemens Winkler
people.bio: German chemist who discovered germanium (1886).

stops.note: Chemist at the Niederpfannenstiel blue-dye works; doctorate Leipzig 1864.
Professor of chemistry and chemical technology.

people.name: Édouard Branly
people.bio: French physicist who invented the coherer, a radio-wave detector.

stops.note: Professor of physics at the Institut Catholique (roster from 1875); academician 1911.

people.name: Marie Curie
people.bio: Polish-French physicist and chemist, pioneer of radioactivity; Nobel laureate in physics (1903) and chemistry (1911).

stops.note: Clandestine Flying University; laboratory training at the Museum of Industry and Agriculture.
Research with Pierre Curie at the School of Physics and Chemistry; doctorate 1903 under Lippmann.
Taught at the École normale supérieure de jeunes filles.
First woman professor at the University of Paris; Radium Institute from 1914.

people.name: Gabriel Lippmann
people.bio: French physicist (colour photography; Nobel 1908) at the Sorbonne.

people.name: Santiago Ramón y Cajal
people.bio: Spanish neuroscientist, founder of the neuron doctrine; Nobel laureate in medicine (1906).

stops.note: Director of the anatomical museum from 1879; doctorate Madrid 1877.
Professor of anatomy; appointed 1883 per sources (roster: 1884).
Professor of histology and pathological anatomy.
Professor of histology at the Central University.

people.name: Theodor Kocher
people.bio: Swiss surgeon of the thyroid gland; Nobel laureate in medicine (1909).

stops.note: Studied medicine under Anton Biermer and Hermann Demme; doctorate 1865.
Followed Biermer to Zurich; influenced by Billroth.
Worked with Henry Thompson and John Erichsen.
Privatdozent and assistant to Georg Lücke.
Professor of surgery and director of the surgical clinic.

people.name: Anton Biermer
people.bio: German internist, professor at Bern, Zurich and Breslau.

people.name: Bernhard von Langenbeck
people.bio: German surgeon, professor at Berlin.

people.name: Franz Brentano
people.bio: German philosopher and psychologist who revived the concept of intentionality.

stops.note: Studied at Munich, Würzburg and Berlin (Aristotle with Trendelenburg); PhD Tübingen 1862.
Habilitation mid-1860s, full professor 1873; then left priesthood and chair.
Settled in Florence as a private scholar.

people.name: Friedrich Adolf Trendelenburg
people.bio: German philosopher and Aristotle scholar at Berlin.

people.name: Edmund Husserl
people.bio: German philosopher who founded phenomenology.

stops.note: Studied astronomy, mathematics, physics and philosophy (Wundt's lectures).

people.name: Carl Stumpf
people.bio: German philosopher and psychologist, student of Brentano, professor at Würzburg, Prague, Halle, Munich and Berlin.

people.name: Wilhelm Wundt
people.bio: German physiologist and philosopher who founded experimental psychology.

stops.note: Medicine at Tübingen and Heidelberg; MD 1856.
Privatdozent; assistant to Helmholtz 1858–65; extraordinary professor 1864.
Professor of philosophy; founded the psychology laboratory 1879.

people.name: Hermann Cohen
people.bio: German-Jewish philosopher, founder of the Marburg school of Neo-Kantianism.

stops.note: Jewish Theological Seminary; also Breslau university.
Philosophy under Trendelenburg; doctorate at Halle.
Taught at the Academy for the Science of Judaism.

people.name: Wilhelm Windelband
people.bio: German philosopher of the Southwest (Baden) school of Neo-Kantianism and historian of philosophy.

stops.note: Studied at Jena (Kuno Fischer), Berlin and Göttingen; Dr. phil. under Lotze 1870.

people.name: Hermann Lotze
people.bio: German philosopher and physiologist at Leipzig and Göttingen.

people.name: Richard Avenarius
people.bio: German-Swiss philosopher who founded empirio-criticism.

stops.note: Studied at Zurich, Berlin and Leipzig; doctorate 1868.

people.name: Henri Bergson
people.bio: French philosopher of duration and creative evolution; Nobel laureate in literature (1927).

stops.note: Taught at the lycée and the university for five years.
Chair of ancient, later modern, philosophy; retired from teaching 1919.

people.name: Émile Durkheim
people.bio: French sociologist who established sociology as an academic discipline.

stops.note: Taught philosophy at provincial lycées (Sens among them).
Studied in Germany at Marburg, Berlin and Leipzig.
Course in social science and pedagogy.
Chair of education at the Sorbonne; full professor 1906; education and sociology 1913.

people.name: Numa Denis Fustel de Coulanges
people.bio: French historian, director of the École Normale Supérieure.

people.name: Émile Boutroux
people.bio: French philosopher who taught at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne.

people.name: Jean Jaurès
people.bio: French socialist leader, philosopher and historian of the French Revolution.

people.name: Alfred Loisy
people.bio: French Catholic priest and biblical scholar, leader of Modernism; excommunicated 1908.

stops.note: Instructor in Hebrew from 1881; theology degree 1890; dismissed 1893.
Chair of the history of religions.

people.name: Louis Duchesne
